    Can you say happy Eid Mubarak?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    Yes, "Eid Mubarak" is the most common and traditional greeting used to wish someone a blessed and happy Eid celebration
    . It translates to "Blessed Eid" or "Blessed Celebration," with "Mubarak" meaning "blessed" and "Eid" referring to the festival. It is appropriate for both Muslims and non-Muslims to use. 
    Common Ways to Use It: 
    • "Eid Mubarak!": The standard, direct greeting.
    • "Happy Eid!": A common English alternative.
    • "Eid Saeed!": Meaning "Happy Eid".
    • "May Allah bless you"
      : Another common variation.
       
    How to Respond:
    If someone says "Eid Mubarak" to you, you can simply reply with: 
    • "Eid Mubarak" (in return).
    • "Khair Mubarak": This wishes goodness upon the person who greeted you.
    • "JazakAllah Khair": Meaning "May Allah reward you with goodness". 
    You can use these greetings throughout both major Islamic holidays: Eid al-Fitr (marking the end of Ramadan) and Eid al-Adha (the festival of sacrifice).

      Can a white person say Eid Mubarak?
      Many Muslims will say Eid Mubarak to people in their community, regardless of their religion. Conversely, if non-Muslims wish Muslims Eid Mubarak, it is almost always happily received. Just try to use it during appropriate times, such as during the celebrations of Eid.
